Bear.characteristics: Large, heavily built mammals with thick fur, strong limbs and long claws.
Bear.habitat: Forests, mountains and tundra, depending on species.
Bear.behavior: Mostly solitary. Usually avoid people but can be dangerous when surprised, protecting cubs or defending food.
Bear.risks: Defensive attacks when surprised or when cubs or food are nearby.
safety: Do not approach, and never get between a bear and its cubs.
Back away slowly while facing the animal; do not run.
Speak calmly so the bear knows you are human.
Secure food and leave the area; report sightings to local wildlife authorities.

Bird.characteristics: Feathered, winged, egg-laying vertebrates; sizes vary widely.
Bird.behavior: Varies widely by species. Some defend nests aggressively.
Bird.risks: Nest-defence swooping, bites or scratches from large birds; birds can carry zoonotic pathogens.
safety: Keep distance from nests and young birds.
Do not handle sick or dead birds with bare hands.
Wash hands after any contact.

Cat.characteristics: Small carnivorous mammal with retractable claws and sharp teeth.
Cat.habitat: Domestic settings; free-roaming and feral populations in many regions.
Cat.behavior: Usually avoids confrontation. May scratch or bite if cornered, frightened or handled.
Cat.risks: Scratches and bites can become infected and need medical care.
safety: Do not corner or grab an unfamiliar cat.
Let it leave on its own.
Clean any scratch or bite thoroughly and seek medical advice.

Cow.behavior: Usually calm, but can be dangerous when protecting calves or when startled.
Cow.risks: Trampling, kicking or crushing, especially near calves or in confined spaces.
safety: Keep your distance and walk around the herd calmly.
Avoid the space between a cow and her calf.
Leave via a fence or gate if the animals approach.

Deer.characteristics: Hoofed ruminants; males of most species carry antlers.
Deer.habitat: Forests, grasslands and wetlands, depending on species.
Deer.behavior: Typically shy. Males in breeding season and mothers with fawns may be aggressive.
Deer.risks: Kicks and antler strikes; road collisions.
safety: Keep a distance, especially from fawns and breeding-season males.
Do not feed or touch wildlife.
Drive carefully at dawn and dusk in deer areas.

Dog.characteristics: Domesticated canid; size, coat and build vary greatly by breed.
Dog.habitat: Human settlements; stray and free-roaming dogs occur worldwide.
Dog.behavior: Varies by individual. Body language, not species, indicates stress or threat. Unfamiliar dogs may be fearful or protective.
Dog.risks: Bites and scratches; bites can transmit infections. A photo cannot show whether a dog is aggressive or has rabies.
safety: Stay calm; avoid sudden movements, shouting and running.
Avoid direct staring; turn side-on and slowly back away.
Do not try to pet, feed or corner an unfamiliar dog.
If bitten, wash the wound with soap and water for several minutes and seek medical care promptly; contact local animal control.

Wolf.characteristics: Large wild canid, often confused with large dogs.
Wolf.habitat: Forests, tundra, grasslands and mountains in parts of North America, Europe and Asia.
Wolf.behavior: Generally avoids humans. Lives in packs.
Wolf.risks: Rare encounters; habituated or provoked animals are a higher risk. Visual confusion with dogs is common.
safety: Keep distance and do not approach.
Do not run; back away slowly while staying upright.
Keep children and pets close and leave the area.
Report sightings to wildlife authorities.

Elephant.characteristics: Largest living land mammals, with trunk and tusks.
Elephant.habitat: Savannas, forests and grasslands in Africa and Asia.
Elephant.behavior: Social and intelligent; can be dangerous when protecting calves, in musth, or when startled.
safety: Keep a large distance; never approach calves.
Stay in a vehicle or behind barriers if possible.
Retreat quietly upwind and out of its path.

Fox.characteristics: Small to medium canid with pointed muzzle and bushy tail.
Fox.habitat: Forests, grasslands, deserts and urban areas.
Fox.behavior: Usually shy and avoids humans. May bite if cornered or handled.
Fox.risks: Bites if handled; can carry parasites and diseases.
safety: Do not feed or approach.
Secure rubbish and pet food.
Seek medical advice after any bite or scratch.

Horse.habitat: Farms, stables and pastures; some feral populations.
Horse.behavior: Prey animal that may kick or bolt when startled.
safety: Approach only from the side where it can see you.
Avoid standing directly behind it.
Move calmly and speak softly.

Kangaroo.characteristics: Marsupial with strong hind legs and tail, native to Australia.
Kangaroo.habitat: Grasslands, scrub and woodland in Australia.
Kangaroo.behavior: Usually avoids people; large males may box or kick if threatened.
Kangaroo.risks: Powerful kicks and claws; road collisions.
safety: Keep a distance and do not feed.
Back away slowly, avoiding eye contact and sudden moves.
Take care driving at dusk and dawn.

Lion.characteristics: Large social big cat; males have manes.
Lion.habitat: African savannas and grasslands; a small population in India.
Lion.risks: Potentially lethal. Do not exit vehicles in wildlife areas.
safety: Stay inside a vehicle or enclosure and follow guide instructions.
Do not run; keep facing the animal and back away slowly if on foot.
Contact wildlife authorities or emergency services.

Panda.characteristics: Bear with black-and-white coat, native to China.
Panda.habitat: Bamboo forests in mountain regions of central China.
Panda.behavior: Solitary; typically avoids people but is a bear and can bite.
safety: Observe only from a distance and follow park rules.
Do not enter enclosures.

Tiger.characteristics: Largest cat species with striped coat.
safety: Do not approach; stay in a vehicle or protected area.
Do not run; back away slowly while facing the animal.
Call emergency services or wildlife authorities.

Zebra.habitat: Savannas and grasslands of eastern and southern Africa.
Zebra.behavior: Herd animal; can kick and bite when threatened.
safety: Keep a distance and never approach or feed.
Stay in vehicles during safaris.
